svg.title: Figure 3. Unsymmetric section: principal axes and the neutral axis
svg.desc: Two panels. (a) A generic unequal-leg angle, 60 by 40 by 5 millimeters, drawn with y up and z to the left, loaded in tension at the outside corner of the tip of its long leg. The section is shaded by normal stress, orange for tension and blue for compression. Dash-dot lines mark the principal axes u (major) and v (minor), which are tilted from the legs. A solid line marks the true neutral axis, which crosses the short leg; a purple dash-dot line, labelled wrong, shows where the neutral axis would be if the product of inertia were ignored. A grey quadrilateral near the centroid is the kern. (b) The second moment of area about an axis at angle theta from z, and the product of inertia in the rotated axes, plotted against theta from minus 90 to 90 degrees: the second moment is largest exactly where the product of inertia is zero, which defines the principal angle theta p.
